capture_tool: capture_transactions.py in this directory, run once as `python3 -I capture_transactions.py https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org .`
notes: walk follows the cursor each getTransactions page returned, 12 pages of 3 from latestLedger - 40, so it records where a real server puts its cursor (the last transaction returned, as toid(ledger, applicationOrder, 1)) and how a page that ends on a ledger's last transaction continues at the next ledger's first

testnet closes ledgers with many transactions, so the walk does not reach the tip; cursor-past-tip and cursor-past-tip-mid-ledger show what a caught-up poller gets instead: an empty page with its own cursor echoed (get_transactions.go in stellar-rpc v30.0.1, the requestCursor comparison)
transactions are summarised to ledger, applicationOrder and txHash plus each page's key sets; error answers are kept whole; response_sha256 is the hash of each raw response body

envelopes are raw bodies posted as written, to record how the server treats the json-rpc envelope itself (scalars, empty and oversized batches, invalid members, notifications); a getNetwork result is reduced to its keys
